title: Annual winter forcing triples the modelled 1997-2012 North Atlantic sigma0 26.5 AOU swings and gives BATS year-to-year timing, but swings stay 2-4 times too small; NP gains do not change (1950-2025)
abstract: Question: the tracer-calibrated near-outcrop ventilation model of sci:dcfc9b0b gave the sign of North Atlantic (NA) AOU changes on sigma0 26.5, but its 1997-2003 rise and 2003-2012 fall on A20/A22 were 5-20 times too small. It was forced with decade-mean winter maps. Is a second process needed, or interannual forcing? Approach: the same model, fields, flow, tracer targets and comparison code, forced with annual late-winter surface sigma0 (WOA23 decadal backbone plus the ERSSTv5-based interannual anomaly of sci:e7f1a165), with original (42) and recalibrated (47) parameter sets, a 199-order shuffle test and a North Pacific (NP) extension; tests written before the runs. Results: the forcing agrees with BATS measured winter density (r = 0.79). The swing ratio |model|/|observed| for the four A20/A22 1997-2012 pairs rose from 0.06 (decadal) to 0.25-0.31 in the best sets (ensemble medians 0.31-0.32; 18 of 42 and 22 of 47 sets >= 0.33, none under decadal forcing), with 4 of 4 signs; the pre-set 0.33 rule failed for the best sets. The recalibrated best set passed the line-pair size test (slope 1.69, r 0.81, 11 of 11 signs). BATS annual r rose from 0.72 to 0.85 and first-difference r from 0.20 to 0.63; no shuffled year order matched (0 of 199). The signal comes from south of 45 N and west of 45 W; the 2010-2011 winters give half of the swing. Sets with full swings over-predict the long-term BATS change. The model AOU follows the observed 26.5 class thickness (r = -0.82), which the fixed-geometry model lacks; thickness explains part of the residual (exploratory). In the NP annual forcing changes regional gains by 0.89-1.11 and leaves the California excess. Limitations: SST-only anomaly, fixed flow and geometry, 11 line pairs, 2-4-fold spread among age-consistent sets.

Observed against model AOU changes for 11 GLODAP line pairs (best sets; diamonds: A20/A22 1997-2003 and 2003-2012), and the 1997-2012 swing ratio over all age-consistent parameter sets for each forcing.
